2369.key_check: Not applicable: the line is itself a sign inventory with no ciphertext to test a key on; the Avignon curial alphabets (DECODE R23, R202-R204) were not compared.
2369.duplicates: known.py on the shelfmark, Durand, Repertorium and Avignon: only this lead; the Borghese secret-script codices already studied (Borgh. 46, 54, 173, Troncarelli 2003) are other volumes.
2369.closed: Seen at native resolution: 22-23 signs with no sign repeated (only two distinct 3-shapes). A Latin or vernacular message of that length would repeat vowels and common letters several times, so the line is a sign alphabet (a cipher alphabet written out without its plain letters, or a pen trial of invented signs), not a message: a key-only specimen with no ciphertext. The hand, a broad-nibbed gothic pen in the brown ink of the period, cannot be dated more closely than the 14th-15th century from the image. The bottom and top margins of ff. 1-54 carry no message in these signs.
